articles.title: Tata Consumer Q2 Results: Net profit rises 16% YoY to Rs 470 crore, revenue up 14%
articles.desc: Tata Consumer Products reported a 16% year-on-year profit increase to Rs 470 crore in Q2 FY27, with revenue rising 14% to Rs 5,661 crore. Strong Indian volumes, salt demand and growth businesses boosted performance, while EBITDA increased 18% to Rs 794 crore.

articles.title: US Stock Market Live Updates: Claude AI parent Anthropic files for IPO; US stock futures steady as oil retreats ahead of earnings, Fed decision
Exporters get six more months of risk cover amid West Asia turmoil
articles.desc: The Centre has extended the RELIEF initiative to March 31, 2027, to assist exporters. This scheme provides risk coverage to exporters facing higher shipping and insurance costs. Eligible exporters can receive 95 percent coverage and protection against rising insurance premiums. Exporters must submit claims through the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation's customer portal to benefit. The extension aims to support trade flows amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

articles.title: Brigade Enterprises signs Hyatt Hotels to manage two hotels in Bengaluru
articles.desc: Brigade Enterprises Ltd has forged a partnership with Hyatt Hotels Corporation to launch two new hotels in Bengaluru, including the Hyatt Regency Bengaluru at Brigade Global Park and an additional property on Whitefield-Kadugodi Road. With a combined total of 600 rooms, this collaboration further enhances Brigade's commitment to developing hospitality within mixed-use spaces, leveraging Bengaluru's strong business travel market for growth.

articles.title: India bonds give up gains as high oil prices weigh
articles.desc: Indian government bonds declined on Monday due to rising oil prices affecting market sentiment and the rupee. The rupee fell for the third consecutive day, adding pressure on bond yields and currency. India's central bank is expected to consider interest rate hikes to stabilize the currency amidst inflation concerns. The Reserve Bank of India has raised its inflation forecast, anticipating a peak of 6% in consumer prices.

articles.title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month
articles.desc: Senior doctors to stage 48-hour walkout, beginning on 25 November, in dispute over pay and pensions.

articles.title: China's central bank sets up non-bank financial institution bond market swap facility
articles.desc: China's central bank has introduced the Bond Market NBFI Swap Facility as of Monday. This initiative is designed to stabilize the bond market amid potential systemic stress or liquidity issues. Bank wealth management subsidiaries and public fund managers will gain access to central bank bills, enabling them to finance the purchase of qualifying bonds or units facing redemption, which can be pledged for central bank support.

articles.title: Bitcoin hovers near $80,000 and Ethereum tests $2,300 as macro and geopolitical risks weigh on crypto markets
articles.desc: Bitcoin traded near $80,000 while Ethereum hovered around $2,327, as macroeconomic uncertainty and geopolitical risks tempered crypto sentiment. Investors monitored Federal Reserve signals, ETF flows, inflation data and options expiry amid cautious technical outlooks and mixed altcoin performance.

articles.title: Funding set to double for plan to get rough sleepers off streets by Christmas
articles.desc: Burnham made ending rough sleeping his first pledge when entering Downing Street in July.

articles.title: ITC Hotels reports revenues of Rs 1054 cr for Q2, PAT at Rs 203 cr
articles.desc: ITC Hotels reported strong second-quarter growth, with revenue rising 26% and net profit increasing 52% year on year, supported by higher room rates, occupancy and demand from business events. The company also expanded its portfolio through new hotel signings, the Welcomhotel Ahmedabad acquisition and a land allotment in Lucknow.

articles.title: China’s proposed solar technology export curbs may delay India’s domestic manufacturing push: Report
articles.desc: China's plan to impose export controls on photovoltaic technologies could create challenges for India's solar manufacturing sector and affect supply chains. These restrictions may lead to delays and increased costs for domestic players aiming for backward integration in manufacturing. The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers Phase II policy timelines could also be disrupted as a result.

articles.title: Key European defence ministers meet in Paris to discuss Ukraine support
articles.desc: Defence ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK to discuss increasing military assistance to Ukraine.

articles.title: Market wrap: Dr Reddys, JSW Steel, Shriram Finance, Tata Consumer top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
articles.desc: Indian equity markets snapped a four-day losing streak as Sensex and Nifty rebounded, supported by broad-based buying. Dr Reddy’s and JSW Steel led gainers, while rising India VIX signalled continued volatility and technical concerns about downside risks.

articles.title: Global Market: European shares flat as investors assess earnings, France turmoil
articles.desc: European shares traded flat as investors weighed corporate earnings and political uncertainty in France. Falling oil prices, driven by hopes of easing US-Iran tensions, supported travel and leisure stocks, while energy shares declined.

articles.title: Asia-focused banks face bond market risks ahead of Q3 earnings
articles.desc: Asia-focused banks face mounting pressure from rising bond yields, inflation and currency volatility ahead of third-quarter earnings. HSBC, Standard Chartered and DBS confront profitability and capital risks, while Japanese and Southeast Asian lenders navigate bond losses, funding pressures and economic uncertainty.

articles.title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow
articles.desc: Marcus Perkins, who owns a hair and beauty salon in Brierley Hill, says he is scared for the future.

articles.title: Ather Energy shares skyrocket 19% after EV maker swings to Rs 1.26 crore profit in Q2
articles.desc: Ather Energy shares surged nearly 19% after the electric two-wheeler maker reported a net profit of Rs 1.26 crore in Q2 FY27, reversing a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 62.8% year-on-year to Rs 1,464 crore, while the company also approved Rs 122 crore in capacity expansion.

articles.title: SoftBank sells 1.21 crore Ola Electric rights entitlements as EV maker seeks to raise Rs 1,000 crore
articles.desc: SoftBank sold nearly 28% of its Ola Electric rights entitlements over two sessions as the company launched a Rs 1,000-crore rights issue. Meanwhile, Motilal Oswal entities applied for 2.39 crore shares amid declining revenue and persistent losses.

articles.title: The war bump is a false victory for S&P 500 profits
articles.desc: The commentary argues that strong S&P 500 earnings growth is narrowly concentrated in AI-linked companies and sectors benefiting from the Iran war, including energy, defence and materials. It warns that higher fuel prices, inflation and borrowing costs could weaken consumer demand, while heavy dependence on the AI boom leaves the market vulnerable if investment returns disappoint.

articles.title: Nirmala Sitharaman reaffirms govt's fiscal discipline push, puts public debt target at 50% of GDP by 2030
articles.desc: FM Sitharaman linked the government's broader economic priorities -- fiscal consolidation, inflation management and currency stability -- with the need to expand employment and enterprise opportunities, particularly for women, through education, skill development and industry participation.

articles.title: Healey to shield low-income pensioners from income tax in the Budget
articles.desc: Changes are needed to prevent the full, flat-rate state pension becoming liable for income tax after it rises in April.

articles.title: How to compare real trading costs across forex trading apps in India
articles.desc: When choosing a forex trading platform, it's important to analyze charges, commissions, and transactional fees. Comparing the overall cost of trade execution is advisable, specifically during peak trading times. For those who trade on the move, testing mobile trading apps for performance and connectivity is vital. Funding and withdrawal charges also affect total expenses, particularly for traders with smaller accounts.

articles.title: US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters
articles.desc: US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies.

articles.title: Rupee weakens for third session as importers step up dollar bids, foreign outflows bite
articles.desc: The Indian rupee declined for three consecutive trading sessions due to increased dollar buying by importers. Elevated oil prices and foreign outflows have contributed to the weakness in the local currency. Brent crude oil prices have risen significantly, raising concerns over inflation and import costs. Foreign investors have been net sellers of Indian equities, adding to market pressures.

articles.title: Moonshot resets subscriber quotas after Kimi K3.1 Pro launch issues
articles.desc: Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI apologised on Monday for rate limiting and unnecessary quota consumption after its Kimi K3.1 Pro launch.

articles.title: India expected to extend duty-free cotton imports through December, sources say
articles.desc: India is expected to extend the 11% customs duty exemption on cotton imports until the end of December to ease supply shortages, lower domestic prices and reduce costs for textile mills. Domestic cotton prices have remained firm amid lower crop prospects, with output estimated below 29 million bales in 2026-27 against demand exceeding 34 million bales.

articles.title: Algeria’s military deployment to Niger: What’s behind the move?
articles.desc: This will be Algeria's first foreign troop deployment in 50 years as the country shifts its military doctrine.

articles.title: Michael Burry's top 10 life lessons for GenZ: 'Buy half the house you can afford'
articles.desc: Michael Burry provides life advice and personal finance tips to a 26-year-old in a Substack post. He emphasizes the importance of exercising, learning, and relationships while advising against gambling. Burry suggests that individuals should invest wisely, specifically recommending to buy half a house they can afford. He warns about the potential for an AI market crash, predicting possible disappointments in revenue.

articles.title: India’s ‘dear friend’ is back in power in Brazil, and a $30 billion trade opportunity is on the table
articles.desc: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Brazilian President-elect Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election, pledging to deepen the India-Brazil Strategic Partnership. Bilateral trade rose 25% to $15.21 billion in 2025, with Lula setting a target of $30 billion.

articles.title: Silver prices are tarnished but not forgotten. Why HSBC thinks gains in white metal may be limited?
articles.desc: Silver prices have plunged nearly 60% from their January record high, but HSBC expects limited gains ahead. The bank sees prices consolidating and edging higher in 2027, supported by gold, while rising mine output, recycling supply, weaker industrial demand, a firm US dollar and elevated yields could cap rallies.

articles.title: Do Palestinians in Gaza expect anything to change after Israel’s election?
articles.desc: After years of war, displacement and restrictions, Gazans ask whether Israel’s election will affect their future.

articles.title: Sumitomo Life to remain cautious on JGB yields, keep investment pace unchanged from H1
articles.desc: Sumitomo Life Insurance will maintain its investment pace for Japanese government bonds in the upcoming months. It intends to carefully monitor yields on super-long Japanese government bonds, assessing any market volatility. The firm expects its JGB holdings to decrease in the Asset Liability Management portfolio by the end of the fiscal year. Predictions suggest that the Bank of Japan will raise its policy rate by December.

articles.title: French bond selloff eases as country spared ratings downgrade
articles.desc: On Monday, the selloff in French government bonds paused after Moody's maintained its rating of Aa3. Weekend protests were mostly peaceful, reducing tensions in the country. France's 10-year OAT yield fell following a rise to its highest level since June 2002. The focus now turns to the European Central Bank's upcoming policy decision on Thursday. Analysts expect the ECB to monitor the rising yields closely and evaluate their impact.

articles.title: Global Market: BOJ nears historic inflation milestone, shifts focus to rate hikes
articles.desc: The Bank of Japan is expected to declare its nearly 14-year battle to achieve 2% inflation successful while keeping interest rates unchanged at 1.25%. With wage growth and inflation expectations strengthening, policymakers may signal further tightening, potentially in December, as they balance persistent price pressures against economic growth and financial stability.

articles.title: ECB Meeting: Five key questions on rates, inflation and Lagarde's exit
articles.desc: The European Central Bank is widely expected to hold interest rates at 2.5% amid elevated energy prices, eurozone inflation and France’s financial instability. With inflation reaching 3.8% in September, markets anticipate further rate hikes. Policymakers will assess economic risks, bond market pressures and leadership changes before signalling future monetary policy decisions.

articles.title: Meta to create non-voting shares to fund AI expansion, retain Zuckerberg’s control
articles.desc: Meta Platforms plans to introduce publicly traded non-voting Class C shares to fund AI investments, acquisitions and employee compensation while preserving Mark Zuckerberg’s voting control. The proposed one-for-one share distribution is expected to begin trading in January 2027.

articles.title: Global equity funds attract $28.16 billion as easing yields boost sentiment
articles.desc: Global equity funds attracted $28.16 billion in weekly inflows as easing US Treasury yields and strong corporate earnings lifted investor sentiment. Asian equities led regional allocations, while technology, bond and precious metals funds also drew fresh investments.

articles.title: Global Market | SK Hynix weighs $12 billion special dividend ahead of Q3 Results: Reports
articles.desc: SK Hynix said it would announce shareholder-return measures alongside its quarterly results amid reports that it was considering a special dividend funded by gains from its Kioxia stake sale. The review comes as investors push major chipmakers to distribute more cash generated by the AI memory boom through dividends and share buybacks.

articles.title: FIIs raise stakes after two quarters of cuts; 8 stocks rally up to 135% in 3 months
articles.desc: Foreign institutional investors turned net buyers in select stocks in the September 2026 quarter after two quarters of reduced exposure. Morepen Laboratories, Shanti Gold International and other stocks gained up to 135% over three months.

articles.title: Swiggy shares jump 5% a day after Q2 results sparked a 17% crash. Why brokerages remain bullish despite target price cuts
articles.desc: Swiggy shares rebounded nearly 5% after plunging 17% following its Q2FY27 results. While food delivery profitability improved, widening Instamart losses prompted Jefferies and Nomura to cut target prices, even as brokerages retained bullish ratings.

articles.title: BSE shares jump over 4% as Motilal Oswal upgrades stock to Buy. 4 reasons behind bullish call
articles.desc: BSE shares rose sharply on Monday after Motilal Oswal upgraded the stock to Buy with a target price of Rs 4,000, implying 23% upside. The brokerage expects strong derivatives volumes, rising premium turnover, improving cash market participation and operating leverage to drive revenue growth, margin expansion and a 27% profit CAGR through FY28.

articles.title: Global Market: China stocks slip as tech shares fall ahead of central bank meetings
articles.desc: Chinese stocks declined as technology shares weakened and investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of major central bank meetings and corporate earnings. Concerns about the AI-driven rally, slowing economic conditions and possible trust-sector selling added to market pressure, while investors watched for support from state-backed funds.

articles.title: Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 9% as Q2 net profit jumps 56% YoY
articles.desc: Apollo Micro Systems has reported an impressive rise in Q2 earnings, with net profit soaring by 56% compared to last year. Revenues spiked 72%, hitting a milestone of Rs 388 crore for the September quarter. The notable increase in EBITDA showcases solid operational efficiency in the defence sector. The company is dedicated to enhancing its capabilities and expanding into global markets, demonstrating a strategic focus on its future objectives.

articles.title: Brazil stock market to crash today? What Lula’s surprise victory in elections means for emerging markets, commodities
articles.desc: Brazil’s stock market faces a potential sharp selloff after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s surprise election victory dashed investor hopes of a change in government and fiscal policy. Analysts warn of possible circuit breakers as the real weakens and soybean futures slide, with emerging markets also watching the fallout.

articles.title: What Bitcoin ETF flows reveal about institutional confidence
articles.desc: US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded volatile inflows and outflows, reflecting uneven investor conviction. Although demand recovered during the third quarter, ETF flows have largely followed Bitcoin’s price movements rather than predicted them, making sustained trends more significant than daily fluctuations.

articles.title: Gold prices rise Rs 700/10 gram; silver gains Rs 1,500/kg ahead of US Fed meet. Key levels to track today
articles.desc: Gold and silver prices rose on the MCX as easing oil prices tempered inflation concerns ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s October 27-28 meeting. Investors will track the Fed’s rate decision, geopolitical developments and the dollar’s movement. Analysts expect volatility, with key support and resistance levels outlined for both precious metals.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan bond yields edge higher ahead of key central bank meetings
articles.desc: Japanese government bond yields edged higher as investors assessed the monetary-policy outlook ahead of meetings by the Bank of Japan and the US Federal Reserve. Markets expected both central banks to keep rates unchanged while monitoring signals about possible December rate increases, inflation and economic growth.

articles.title: Knighting Sinfield 'easiest decision anyone's had to make,' says Prince William
articles.desc: The rugby league star is "gold dust" and "should have been Sir Kevin years ago," says the Prince of Wales.

articles.title: Tonbo Imaging shares soar another 17% after a 64% listing pop. Buy, sell or hold the stock?
articles.desc: Tonbo Imaging shares rallied after a strong stock market debut, following heavy demand for its IPO. Investors will track revenue growth, order execution, profitability, working capital and cash flows to assess the defence electronics company’s long-term prospects.

articles.title: $7.7 trillion AI bet: Can hyperscalers earn enough to justify the spending?
articles.desc: Six major hyperscalers are projected to spend $7.7 trillion on AI between 2026 and 2030, but generating adequate returns will be a challenge. UBS estimates they need $1 trillion in additional earnings before interest and taxes by 2031. The key questions are whether AI boosts productivity and companies can monetise those gains.

articles.title: Jio’s record India IPO falls short of record payday for bankers
articles.desc: Jio Platforms raised about $3.1 billion through its record IPO, but intense competition among investment banks kept fees relatively low at around 0.65% of the issue size.

articles.title: Oil, US Treasuries prop up Indian bonds
articles.desc: Indian government bonds increased in early trading as oil prices declined, following a previous rally. The Brent crude price slipped significantly after hitting a six-month high last week, which impacted the debt market. Foreign investors have sold a substantial amount of Indian government debt since August, contributing to a prolonged rise in benchmark yields. Concerns over inflation and the Reserve Bank of India's rate decisions are influencing market sentiments.

articles.title: From Carnegie to Claude: AI wealth could reshape philanthropy
articles.desc: A wave of American wealth created by artificial intelligence companies could produce some of the largest charitable sums since the era of Andrew Carnegie and John D. Rockefeller, raising questions about where the money goes. Nan Ransohoff of payments firm Stripe has described the moment as a "third wave" of American philanthropy, after the industrial fortunes of the late 19th century and the internet billionaires of recent decades.

articles.title: Big Tech Earnings Week: Will AI spending pay off?
articles.desc: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report quarterly results in a crucial week for AI stocks. Investors will track cloud growth, profit margins, free cash flow and infrastructure spending to assess whether surging AI demand can justify massive investments.

articles.title: Bharat Coking Coal shares rally 5% after Q2 profit turnaround; revenue jumps 39% YoY
articles.desc: Bharat Coking Coal shares sharply on Monday after the Coal India subsidiary reported a turnaround to profit in Q2 FY27, with net profit at Rs 123.7 crore and revenue up 39% year-on-year to Rs 4,412.58 crore. However, first-half production declined, while technical indicators pointed to continued weakness in the stock.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan's Nikkei falls for third straight session as chip stocks slide
articles.desc: Japan's Nikkei share average slipped for a third straight session on Monday, primarily due to declines in chip-related stocks. The Nikkei 225 saw a decrease of 0.43%, contrasted by a 0.48% rise in the broader Topix index. Despite a surge in energy stocks driven by rising oil prices, concerns over global market fluctuations left investors wary.

articles.title: 5 global market themes to watch out for this week
articles.desc: Global markets face a pivotal week as major central banks announce policy decisions, Big Tech companies report earnings, and political developments in Britain, Israel and Brazil unfold. China's leadership meeting will also draw attention amid trade tensions and weak domestic demand.

articles.title: US stocks face crucial test as AI earnings, Fed meeting loom
articles.desc: US stocks face a crucial week as earnings from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon coincide with the Federal Reserve’s policy decision. Investors will assess whether massive AI investments can deliver sustainable returns, while the Fed’s guidance on interest rates and uncertainty surrounding the November midterm elections could shape market sentiment and volatility.

articles.title: Sensex jumps 1,100 pts from day’s low, Nifty closes above 22,750 as D-St rebounds after 4-day losses. Is this relief rally sustainable?
articles.desc: On Monday, the Indian stock market experienced a notable rebound, with the Sensex and Nifty indices recovering about 2% after previous declines. Major players like Kotak Mahindra Bank and Adani Ports contributed to this surge, boosting investor confidence. However, analysts caution against potential risks due to rising crude oil prices and economic uncertainties, indicating that while there's room for recovery, careful stock selection remains essential.

articles.title: Rupee falls 5 paise to 94.98 against US dollar in early trade
articles.desc: In early trading, the rupee was priced at 94.98 against the US dollar, slipping by 5 paise primarily due to high crude oil rates and ongoing geopolitical conflicts. Despite the dollar index facing a slight decline of 0.15 percent, India's forex reserves have seen a downturn, potentially affecting the currency's stability. However, the Reserve Bank of India's timely intervention might bolster the rupee at lower trading levels.

articles.title: Holcim lifts guidance again on strong demand
articles.desc: Holcim has increased its full-year guidance due to robust demand for sustainable building materials. The company reported a 17% jump in recurring Ebit in the third quarter, surpassing expectations. Increased customer demand and cost discipline contributed significantly to this profit increase. The firm aims to announce around 15 acquisitions by the end of this year. Holcim is focusing on alternative fuels to mitigate rising energy costs.

articles.title: AU Small Finance Bank shares tumble 10% after Q2 results, but Jefferies and Motilal see up to 37% upside
articles.desc: AU Small Finance Bank shares fell up to 10% despite a 53% year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit. Jefferies and Motilal Oswal retained Buy ratings, citing growth prospects, improving asset quality and lower credit costs.

articles.title: Shriram Finance shares crash 6% as Jefferies, Citi, and other brokerages slash target prices after Q2 results. Why do they still say ‘Buy’?
articles.desc: Shriram Finance shares fell sharply on Monday after Jefferies, Citi and Motilal Oswal cut their target prices following the NBFC’s Q2 results. Despite concerns over rising credit costs and rural stress, all three brokerages retained their ‘Buy’ ratings, citing strong net interest income, resilient margins and long-term growth potential.

articles.title: Paras Healthcare allotment likely today: Check GMP, key details and how to check status
articles.desc: Paras Healthcare IPO allotment is expected to be finalised today after the Rs 1,450-crore issue was subscribed 2.23 times. With the GMP indicating a potential listing gain of around 1%, investors can check their allotment status on the MUFG Intime, NSE and BSE websites. The hospital chain is scheduled to list on October 28, 2026, after reporting a return to profitability in FY26.

articles.title: Coforge slips 3% even as Jefferies, Nomura, others raise targets after Q2 earnings. Why are they bullish?
articles.desc: Coforge shares fell despite strong Q2 results and brokerages raising target prices. Net profit surged 56.5% year-on-year to Rs 588.1 crore, while revenue jumped 54% to Rs 6,170.8 crore. EBITDA rose 67% to Rs 1,269.7 crore, with margins expanding 168 basis points to 20.6%. The company raised its FY27 EBIT margin guidance to 16%, while its 12-month order book grew 45% to $2.38 billion.

articles.title: Japanese companies compensate users as cyberattacks buffet economy
articles.desc: GMO Internet Group said customers would be compensated for losses stemming from unauthorised access following a cyberattack on its foreign exchange trading service, and all customers would receive 5,000 yen ($32) as "an initial gesture of good faith," CEO Masatoshi Kumagai said in a blog post on Sunday.

articles.title: Talent, compute and R&D key to India's AI ambitions: Report
articles.desc: India will need to strengthen its talent pool, research and development (R&D) capabilities, computing infrastructure and data systems to translate advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies into economic and social benefits, according to a report by KPMG.

articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX raised $40 billion in debt for GPUs
articles.desc: Musk's post comes after Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX is in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion for the purchase of ​Nvidia artificial intelligence chips.

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude accessed Georgia state vote count information behind paywall
articles.desc: Anthropic's Claude bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available US state of Georgia voter data without human authorization, Axios reported on Sunday.

articles.desc: Chancellor John Healey will set out his plans for UK taxes on 28 October.

articles.desc: Data centres are the lifeblood of our digital world, but there are growing concerns about their environmental impact. The BBC explores their rise in charts.

articles.title: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
articles.desc: After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming, writes Lucy Williamson.

articles.title: Ind AS 118: India Inc gears up for big changes to financial reporting
articles.desc: India’s largest companies are preparing for the implementation of Ind AS 118, which may impact financial reporting. Changes include new classifications for income and expenses, and new operating profit reporting methods. Companies face challenges due to complex requirements and the need for system adjustments. Audit committees are discussing transition plans while awaiting final rules and guidance from regulatory bodies.

articles.desc: Individuals will be hired for positions at both CCI and its investigation arm, the director general (DG) office, according to public notices.

articles.desc: I know many of you are mourning the loss of the Arc browser, and I get it. It felt like the first app in a long time to really offer a new approach to browser design. articles.title: ‘Very high’ expectations from India-EU FTA, says Rotterdam port chief
articles.desc: Boudewijn Siemons, CEO of the Port of Rotterdam, expressed high expectations for the India-EU free trade agreement. He highlighted the importance of collaboration between ports and nations to facilitate global trade. Siemons conveyed his optimism about increased business opportunities between Europe and India. Negotiations for the free trade agreement have concluded, with hopes to sign it by year-end. The implementation of the agreement is anticipated for next year.

articles.title: Gabon says access to social media restored after eight-month ban
articles.desc: The authorities had justified the ban by saying online content was fuelling conflict, while the opposition had condemned it as an abuse of power.

articles.title: Cities cannot be governed from state capitals, need empowered local governments: NITI Aayog's Rajiv Gauba
articles.desc: Rajiv Gauba emphasized the need for reforms in urban governance during the National Urban Conclave. He highlighted the importance of empowering city governments and proposed directly elected mayors for better governance. The projected increase in India's urban population demands significant infrastructure and service management changes. Gauba called for improved municipal revenues and the adoption of the Model Tenancy Act to support affordable housing.
